Patient-reported symptoms:

  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Friends: avoid seeing friends, Sit With Back to Wall: always sit with back against a wall to see the room, Checking Surroundings: constantly scan environment for signs of threat
  Threat: Alert at Home: I feel on guard even inside my own home, Startle to Sounds: I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people, Startle Response: Feeling jumpy or easily startled
  Memory: Vivid Memory: My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed., Visual Memories: My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images., Uncontrolled Access: The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to

Vignette:
Kai had always been a man who loved his routine, and after 40 years in the publishing industry, he knew every nook and cranny of his office building. But on that fateful night five years ago, when the warehouse next door caught fire and raged out of control, burning down half the block, Kai's world was forever changed. He remembered the smell of smoke and alcohol from the nearby bars wafting through the air as he watched helplessly from across the street. As the flames engulfed the buildings, Kai couldn't shake off the feeling that he should have done something to prevent it. The guilt lingered long after the fire was extinguished, leaving him with a sense of unease that followed him everywhere. He would wake up in the middle of the night, drenched in sweat, with vivid images of burning buildings and screaming people still etched in his mind. The nightmares became more frequent over time, and Kai started avoiding social gatherings, afraid of what he might say or do if memories of that night resurfaced. His friends noticed his absence but couldn't understand why Kai was suddenly pulling away. "I'm just busy with work," he'd tell them, but deep down, he knew it was more than that. Kai started taking precautions to ensure his safety in public spaces. He would always choose a seat with his back against the wall, scanning the room for any signs of potential threats. His colleagues grew accustomed to seeing him sit in the same spot during meetings, and while they thought it was just a quirk, Kai knew he needed to be vigilant. The smell of alcohol had become particularly potent as a trigger. One whiff would transport him back to that terrible night, and he'd feel like he was reliving the whole ordeal all over again. He started avoiding bars and restaurants where his friends liked to hang out, opting instead for quiet nights at home with his wife. But even in the safety of his own home, Kai couldn't shake off the feeling of being on guard. He would constantly scan the surroundings, checking locks and windows, making sure everything was secure before he could relax. His wife, Mele, had grown concerned about his behavior but didn't know how to reach him. "It's like I'm always waiting for something bad to happen," Kai told her one evening as they sat in their living room. "I just can't seem to turn it off." The sound of a car backfiring outside made him jump, and Mele saw the fear flash across his face before he composed himself. As time went by, Kai's behavior became more erratic. He would startle at ordinary sounds that wouldn't bother most people – a knock on the door, the rustling of leaves outside. His reactions were becoming more intense, and it was taking a toll on his relationship with Mele. One evening, as they were watching TV together, a news report about a warehouse fire flashed on the screen. Kai's eyes widened, and he felt like he'd been punched in the gut. The memories came flooding back – vivid images of flames engulfing buildings, people running for their lives. He excused himself and went to bed early, feeling overwhelmed. The next morning, Mele sat him down and said, "Kai, I think it's time you got help. This can't go on forever." Kai knew she was right. The nightmares were getting worse, the memories more intrusive. He couldn't keep living like this, constantly on edge, waiting for something to happen. As they made an appointment with a therapist, Kai felt a glimmer of hope that he hadn't felt in years. Maybe, just maybe, he could learn to let go of some of these burdens and find his way back to the man he used to be.
